answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so influence must be reached along short, independently supported paths rather than asserted by identity count. A Sybil grove can spiral into apparent density internally, yet its sparse external cut gives it low conductance, leaving few paths to wander across that boundary. Under a voting rule weighted by walk reachability, conductance and min-cut bounds therefore cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight by its trusted links, limiting the sway of fabricated membership.
